stemMd: A journal corrects an article whenever a factual mistake changes its main conclusion. It retracts an article only if deliberate deception is established. A factual mistake changes an article's main conclusion, but no deception has been established. What does the policy require?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Leave it unchanged because deception has not been established.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Retract every article by the same author.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Correct it only if the author agrees.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Correct the article, and do not retract it on the stated facts.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Retract it because every changed conclusion establishes deception.

explanationMd: Correction is triggered by the consequential factual error. Retraction has a separate necessary condition—established deception—which is absent. Do not transfer the condition for one response to the other.

distractorRationale.b: The rule provides no collective sanction.
distractorRationale.e: A mistaken conclusion does not establish intent.
distractorRationale.a: Correction does not require deliberate deception.
distractorRationale.c: Author consent is not a condition in the policy.
